title: `<link rel="stylesheet">` that were script blocking during page load later block main thread when rel is set to `stylesheet` again
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

While working on making Servo pass all tests in `/html/semantics/document-metadata/the-link-element/`, I run into two tests that seem to have confusing behavior that also appears to be unspecced.

Relevant tests:
- https://wpt.fyi/results/html/semantics/document-metadata/the-link-element/link-rel-attribute.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned which updates `rel` with various steps
- https://wpt.fyi/results/html/semantics/document-metadata/the-link-element/link-rel-attribute-tokenization.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned which updates `rel` like the other test, but this time with multiple space separated values

According to the spec, the behavior of these two should be equivalent, since invalid values for `rel` and whitespace is ignored. ~~However, Chrome passes the first one and fails the second one.~~ (Chrome now passes both after https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/7765667)

That said, browsers also do something different when running the tests. The number of times that `/html/semantics/document-metadata/the-link-element/resources/link-rel-attribute.css` is loaded (same in both tests):

| Browser | # of requests                            |
|---------|------------------------------|
| Chrome  | 1                            |
| Firefox | 2                            |
| Webkit  | 1 |

What is not clear to me:
1. Why do Chromium/Webkit not refetch when the `rel` is set again? The resource could have changed in between the initial fetch and the second one, or cookies could have changed, etc...
2. Why do all browsers block the currently executing script when the attribute is set? I don't see anything related to that in the spec. There is the case of script blocking during page load (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#script-blocking-style-sheet-set), but as I read the spec is no longer relevant after the page has completed loading.

To me, it seems bad to block the main thread on such a refetch. Instead, I would expect such requests to be asynchronous and thus not immediately visible in the currently executing script. Therefore, I would have expected this test to update the attribute and then (if the link is applicable) wait for the `load` event before checking if the style is `rgb(0, 128, 0)`

I tried to figure out where in the respective browser engines this was implemented, but unfortunately couldn't find anything. The implementations appear to follow the spec, yet behave differently.

My proposal would be to update the WPT test to wait for `load` events and also expect it to fetch the resource twice (or however many times is relevant for when the link is valid).
